market_mood: The Iran war keeps tightening energy markets — record refining margins, record tanker attacks in Hormuz and another EIA price-forecast hike — while Treasury yields at 24-year highs quietly pressure anything rate-sensitive.
self_check: My oil & energy and rates calls have been the most reliable (around 77-78% right), while single-stock merger and defense ideas have been hit-or-miss, so today leans on energy supply-shock plays and one clear AI-power contract.

picks.reason: Attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest weekly level since the Iran war began, which raises war-risk premiums and spot tanker rates — a direct earnings boost for crude tanker owners.

Shell flagged record refining margins from the Iran war, and Northeast politicians are complaining about surging heating oil — both signs refiners' diesel and fuel cracks are unusually fat this quarter.
Record jet fuel and refining margins mean airlines pay far more for fuel; American has the most debt and thinnest margins, so a fuel-driven reality check ahead of airline earnings hits it hardest.
Alphabet locked in a 20-year, $4.3bn nuclear power supply deal with Constellation for AI data centers, adding long-dated, high-visibility cash flow as power demand from AI keeps climbing.

Treasury yields are at a 24-year high and India just joined the global tightening wave, which raises borrowing costs and pressures property valuations; real estate is already the weakest sector this week.
TD SYNNEX agreed to acquire BlueStar, expanding its specialty IoT and mobility distribution; tuck-in deals like this tend to be digested slowly by the market.

watchlist_notes.note: Record high Tuesday but a big bearish put spread and 24-year-high yields show the rally is being doubted.
AI spending news stays supportive, though higher long-term rates are a headwind for richly valued tech.
Mixed session with Caterpillar swinging the index both ways this week; no new macro driver.
Only commentary pieces debating whether its AI story is underrated; no hard news today.
No major company news; the broader story is AI capex and whether rising rates squeeze valuations.
Stock hit a fresh high on AI demand headlines, so the good news is largely in the price already.
AWS growth is strong but heavy capex spending keeps investors cautious; no new news today.
Signed a 20-year, $4.3B nuclear power deal with Constellation, but Finland ordered two of its data centers halted.
Joining Alphabet in a $300M AI-biology investment at Biohub — small money, long-term optionality.
Reuters reports Tesla pressured European regulators over FSD approval, a possible regulatory headache.
Tops the Evident AI index and is building stablecoin reserve infrastructure; high yields help net interest income.
Gold slipped as the dollar firmed and investors wait on Fed minutes.
Long bond prices under pressure with 10-year yields at a 24-year high.

top_buys.pitch: Record attacks on tankers in Hormuz push war-risk premiums and spot rates higher, straight to tanker owners' bottom line.
top_buys.why: Reuters reports tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz were the highest of any week since the Iran war started. When shipping gets dangerous, insurance and freight rates spike and voyages get rerouted, lengthening ton-miles — both good for crude tanker earnings. Frontline is a pure-play crude tanker owner with high operating leverage to spot rates, and the market often underreacts to rate moves until quarterly results confirm them.
top_buys.risks: A sudden Iran de-escalation or ceasefire would deflate war-risk premiums fast, and tanker stocks are volatile and can give back gains in days.
top_buys.watch: Weekly VLCC/Suezmax spot rate prints and any Iran nuclear negotiation headlines.

top_buys.pitch: Shell says refining margins are at records; the largest US refiner should print a strong quarter.
top_buys.why: Shell guided to record refining margins because the Iran war has disrupted fuel supply, and Northeast lawmakers are publicly complaining about surging heating oil costs — a sign distillate cracks are extremely wide. Marathon is the biggest US refiner with heavy distillate exposure and returns most of its free cash via buybacks. Refining margin strength tends to show up in earnings over weeks, not in one headline pop.
top_buys.risks: Crude spiking faster than product prices would compress margins, and a quick peace deal could normalize cracks.
top_buys.watch: Weekly EIA distillate inventories and Q3 refining results later this month.

top_buys.pitch: Record fuel cracks are an airline cost shock, and the most leveraged US carrier feels it most.
top_buys.why: The same record refining margins that help refiners are a direct cost increase for airlines, since jet fuel is priced off those cracks. Analysts are already flagging a 'fuel-driven reality check' ahead of airline Q3 results. American carries the heaviest debt load and thinnest margins among big US carriers, so each dollar of fuel hurts its earnings more.
top_buys.risks: Strong travel demand or an oil pullback on Iran de-escalation could let airlines pass costs through and rally the group.
top_buys.watch: Delta's Q3 report this week as the sector read-through, plus jet fuel crack spreads.

top_buys.pitch: A 20-year, $4.3bn nuclear supply deal with Google adds durable AI-driven cash flow.
top_buys.why: Alphabet agreed to buy carbon-free nuclear power from Constellation for its AI data centers over 20 years. These contracts lock in high-margin, long-dated revenue and validate nuclear as the preferred power source for AI, which supports a higher valuation over time. Utilities were the best-performing sector this week, showing money is already rotating toward AI power.
top_buys.risks: Utilities have run hard and are sensitive to rising bond yields, which are at 24-year highs; much of the AI-power theme may be priced in.
top_buys.watch: Further hyperscaler power purchase agreements and Constellation's next earnings update.

top_buys.pitch: With the 10-year at a 24-year high, property values and REIT financing costs face real pressure.
top_buys.why: Treasury yields hitting levels unseen since 2002 raise the cost of refinancing debt-heavy REITs and make their dividend yields less attractive versus risk-free bonds. India joining the global tightening wave shows the direction of travel is still higher rates abroad too. Real estate is already the only sector down over the past week, suggesting the trend is intact rather than exhausted.
top_buys.risks: Dovish Fed minutes or a flight to safety could pull yields down quickly and spark a sharp REIT bounce.
top_buys.watch: Fed minutes and the 10-year Treasury yield.

summary.big_story: The Iran war keeps squeezing energy markets — record Hormuz tanker attacks, record refining margins and higher EIA price forecasts — while 24-year-high Treasury yields pressure rate-sensitive assets.
summary.top_pick: Frontline, because record tanker attacks in Hormuz push war-risk premiums and spot tanker rates higher, which flows straight into tanker owners' earnings.
summary.watch: Fed minutes for rate clues, Delta's results as the first read on airline fuel costs, and any escalation headlines out of Iran or Yemen.
